items.text: How much warmer are city centres than their suburbs at night?
Which surface features explain the difference?
items.detail: Tree cover, roof albedo, road density

items.text: What has worked where cities intervened?
items.detail: Cool-roof and tree programmes in Phoenix, Chicago, Atlanta

slides.title: Night-time gaps reach 4 °C in Phoenix
slides.subtitle: Mean summer night temperature difference, city centre minus suburb, 2015–2025.
slides.source: [1] NOAA ISD station pairs; our calculation.
slides.insight:
Phoenix has the least tree cover of the three and the most paved surface.

Atlanta's gap has narrowed since its 2019 tree ordinance.
slides.callout: The gap is largest where there is the least shade.

slides.title: Heat is stored, not just received
slides.subtitle: The mechanism in one sentence.
slides.text: "Dark roofs and asphalt absorb heat all day and release it after sunset, so the city cools hours later than the countryside."
slides.source: [2] Oke 1982, Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society.
